Every value in `charts/assayd/values.yaml`, its default, and what the chart says about it.

Chart version **0.1.0**, appVersion **0.1.0**. The chart version IS the platform version, and the
appVersion is the operator image tag.

The prose under each key is the comment that sits above it in `values.yaml`, reproduced rather
than re-written — so this page cannot say something the file does not. Where a comment explains why
a default is what it is, or what breaks when it is changed, that is the chart's own text.

Defaults are the values as written, which is the **prod profile at the core tier**. The chart also
ships `charts/assayd/values-local.yaml`; the keys it overrides are listed at the end.

The file opens by saying:

## `tier`

**Default:** `core`

tier: core | plus

```
 core  — the engine: what is needed to run governed agents.
 plus  — adds Argo Workflows, Phoenix, OpenFGA, eval runner images.
```

Only `core` is implemented; `plus` is rejected at render rather than silently ignored, because a values file that appears to take effect and does not is worse than one that errors.

## `profile`

**Default:** `prod`

profile: prod | local

```
 prod  — replicas, anti-affinity, PDBs.
 local — single replica everything, local-path storage; the honest mode.
```

## `operator`

A group of 10 key(s).

### `operator.image`

A group of 4 key(s).

#### `operator.image.repository`

**Default:** `ghcr.io/quinyte/assayd-operator`

#### `operator.image.tag`

**Default:** `0.1.0`

Pinned, never floating: a rollout that cannot be reproduced is not a rollout.

#### `operator.image.digest`

**Default:** `""`

A digest WINS over the tag when set, and the release workflow sets it to the digest it published and cosign-signed. A tag can be repointed at other content after signing; a digest names the content itself, which is the same rule assayd's admission applies to agent images (ADR-0019).

Verify what you are about to run:

```
 cosign verify ghcr.io/quinyte/assayd-operator@<digest> \
   --certificate-identity-regexp '^https://github.com/Quinyte/assayd/' \
   --certificate-oidc-issuer https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com
```

#### `operator.image.pullPolicy`

**Default:** `IfNotPresent`

### `operator.replicas`

**Default:** `2`

Two at the prod profile: the operator is leader-elected, so a standby takes over on node failure rather than waiting for a reschedule. The local profile forces this to 1 regardless.

The standby is never Ready, by design: readiness means "this process is reconciling" (cmd/operator's "reconciling" readyz check waits for the lease). With 2, `helm install --wait` and `kubectl rollout status` never complete, because the Deployment stays at 1/2 available. Use profile local, or wait for one Ready operator Pod instead.

### `operator.leaderElection`

**Default:** `true`

Leader election is on by default. The chart grants the leases permission it needs; without that grant controller-runtime retries a forbidden lease forever while the pod reports Ready and reconciles nothing.

### `operator.evalSuiteCheckInterval`

**Default:** `30s`

How long a cached answer to "is the EvalSuite CRD installed?" may persist before the next reconcile re-checks it. This bounds the cache, not the agent.

### `operator.podDisruptionBudget`

A group of 2 key(s).

Disruption budget, prod profile only. maxUnavailable rather than minAvailable: with N replicas a minAvailable of N permits no eviction at all, so `kubectl drain` hangs and routine node maintenance becomes an incident.

#### `operator.podDisruptionBudget.enabled`

**Default:** `true`

#### `operator.podDisruptionBudget.maxUnavailable`

**Default:** `1`

### `operator.affinity`

**Default:** `{}`

Left empty on purpose: the template renders a soft anti-affinity by default so both replicas do not land on one node. Setting this replaces it, which is the right escape hatch for a cluster with its own topology rules.

## `namespace`

**Default:** `assayd-system`

The namespace the operator runs in. CRs may live anywhere. Agent WORKLOADS and revision material do not live where the Agent does: the operator creates one `assayd-run-<agent-namespace>` per namespace that holds an Agent (design 02 A42), and keeps its binding records here.

## `gateway`

A group of 6 key(s).

The agentgateway subchart is not shipped yet (design 07 A1): P1 is the declared-ungoverned tier. The Gateway's name is fixed here because the route-authoring admission policy (design 07 A5.9) must know it before the Gateway exists, so that the first route anyone authors against it is already governed.

### `gateway.enabled`

**Default:** `false`

false -- what P1 ships -- means the operator emits NOTHING at the gateway and puts GovernanceSkipped=GatewayDisabled on every Agent (design 03 3.1).

true runs design 03's first slice. The operator emits each Agent's serving HTTPRoute, into the run namespace, attached to the Gateway named below, and for a NEW Agent whose spec.expose.a2a.auth is apikey or absent, its `<agent>-auth` AgentgatewayPolicy: API keys from the ConfigMaps labelled assayd.dev/api-keys: "true" in the run namespace, admitting the group named for the Agent's namespace. That route is published only after an anonymous request through it gets 401, so `servingUrl` below is required. auth: none is published at once, unauthenticated, and says so. No AgentgatewayBackend is emitted and no budget, rate limit or tool allowlist is enforced.

The Gateway API CRDs must be installed: with this true and them absent the operator refuses to start rather than reporting everything is fine. The chart does not install them and neither does it ship a Gateway (A1).

### `gateway.name`

**Default:** `assayd`

The Gateway an emitted route's parentRef names. Fixed here because the route-authoring admission policy must know it before the Gateway exists.

The LISTENER is not configurable: an emitted route always attaches to the listener named `http` (design 07 A5.3), because nothing in this chart renders a Gateway and there is no value to read one from. Name your listener something else and every route reports `NoMatchingParent`, and anonymous requests 404. The operator reads route status (Accepted, ResolvedRefs) only while a Create or Lock is in flight, so a NEW Agent says so: an API-key Agent at once, Ready=False with reason AuthEnforcementPending, and an auth: none Agent after about four minutes of Ready=True. Both then report PolicyApplyIncomplete, reason AuthEnforcementUnverified, naming NoMatchingParent. An Agent ALREADY SERVED is reported too, since design 03 A80: it reads Ready=False, phase Degraded and PolicyApplyIncomplete, reason ServingRouteNotAccepted, naming the Gateway's own condition, with status.auth.routeRefused recording the claim; restore the listener and it clears and returns to Ready. Renaming the listener also leaves <agent>-auth attached to nothing, so GovernanceSkipped reads AuthPolicyNotAttached at the same time; the route is the cause the other three name, because nothing reaches the agent at all. Measured on agentgateway 1.5.0, by walking it through on k3d against this operator (docs/research/a80-served-route-walkthrough-2026-09.md).

`http` is also the listener assayd-gateway-routes keeps for the operator alone: admission.toolRouteWriters, below, may attach routes to any other listener of this Gateway, and never to it (design 07 A6.15).

### `gateway.url`

**Default:** `""`

The base URL an agent's EGRESS traverses -- where it sends MCP tool calls. The operator injects it into every agent as ASSAYD_GATEWAY_URL (design 02 11), after the user's own env, so an Agent cannot override the variable (admission also refuses the ASSAYD_ prefix). That is ALL it guarantees: nothing restricts where an agent's egress actually goes. Empty -- the default -- injects nothing. It is a URL an agent dials, so it must name a listener that admits the tool routes (the e2e harness uses the Gateway's `tools` listener); nothing checks that it does.

### `gateway.servingUrl`

**Default:** `""`

The base URL of the Gateway's SERVING listener -- the one each Agent's `<agent>-serving` route attaches to (listener `http`), and NOT `url` above, which names the listener agents send egress to. Design 03 3.3.3 sends the compiler's anonymous `401` probe here, with the Agent's Host header.

Rendered as --gateway-serving-url. REQUIRED whenever `enabled` is true: the chart refuses to render without it, and the operator refuses to start. The policy compiler publishes a new Agent's route only after an anonymous request sent HERE, with the Agent's Host header, gets 401. The operator refuses a value that is not an absolute http(s) URL naming only a host and port, and checks nothing else. A URL that reaches no listener holds every new Agent unpublished, and its Agents say so. A URL that reaches a different listener, a proxy, or anything that answers 401 on its own, or a Gateway carrying a Gateway-level auth policy, can answer the 401 the Agent's own policy did not, and nothing detects that: design 03 §3.3.3 records it as open, and §8.1 owes the conformance case on the `http` listener.

### `gateway.namespace`

**Default:** `""`

The namespace the Gateway object lives in, which is NOT the namespace the operator runs in. Design 03 3.2 puts gateway-scoped resources in "the gateway's own namespace", and agentgateway forces the separation anyway: its v1.5.0 proxy sets no seccompProfile and AgentgatewayParameters cannot supply one, so the proxy cannot run in assayd-system, which the chart enforces as PodSecurity `restricted`.

This is load-bearing, not cosmetic. assayd-gateway-routes reserves route authorship by comparing the parentRef's namespace to THIS value; point it at the wrong namespace and the reservation matches nothing and silently permits any identity to attach a route. Measured: moving the Gateway out of assayd-system while this read `.Values.namespace` let an ordinary test identity attach one.

Empty means `.Values.namespace` above -- the namespace the OPERATOR runs in, which is where a single-namespace install puts everything. It is NOT the Helm release namespace: hack/e2e.sh installs the release into `default` while the operator runs in `assayd-system`, so this default must not be read as "wherever you helm-installed to".

With gateway.enabled, the chart also renders a Role and RoleBinding IN this namespace (the operator's read of the gateway's NACK Events, design 03 3.3), so it must exist before `helm install`, or the install fails.

### `gateway.hostnameSuffix`

**Default:** `assayd.internal`

The suffix appended to `<agent>.<agent-namespace>` to form the hostname the emitted serving route matches. NO DESIGN SETTLES THIS: design 03 3.2 fixes where the route lives and what names the object and says nothing about the host it matches, so this is assayd's choice and it is configurable rather than presented as the design's.

It is a ROUTING KEY, matched against the request's Host header -- not an address. Nothing in this chart creates DNS for it, so reaching an agent by this name from outside the cluster needs a record an administrator provides. `.internal` is ICANN-reserved for private use, so it cannot collide with a name anyone can register.

Set here rather than left to the binary's own default, and the template renders the flag only when this is non-empty -- so an overlay that replaces the whole `gateway:` map falls back to the operator's compiled-in default instead of passing it an empty string.

## `admission`

A group of 3 key(s).

Design 07 A5.9: the identities permitted to write the reserved assayd.dev namespace labels. The operator's own ServiceAccount is always permitted; list the tenant-operator's here when the enterprise module is installed. Every identity added is a principal that can mint a SPIFFE-selected namespace — keep it to assayd's own controllers.

### `admission.extraOperators`

**Default:** `[]`

### `admission.apiKeyWriters`

A group of 2 key(s).

Design 03 3.4.4: who may write a ConfigMap labelled `assayd.dev/api-keys` in a run namespace. Such a ConfigMap holds API-key hashes, and agentgateway reads them live, so writing one mints a principal. The design says the key set "is written by an administrator"; this names the administrators. The operator's own ServiceAccount (and extraOperators) are always permitted.

`system:masters` is the default because it is the one group this reservation could not exclude anyway: its members bypass RBAC and can delete the policy's binding. Every other administrator must be listed here, by username or by group -- a `cluster-admin` binding alone is NOT enough, and kubeadm (and so kind) puts its admin kubeconfig in `kubeadm:cluster-admins`, not `system:masters`. Each identity added can mint a principal for any Agent's group.

Never list a group every identity carries, such as `system:authenticated` or `system:serviceaccounts`: this reservation is only the writer check, so it would then refuse no one, and any identity with ConfigMap RBAC in a run namespace could mint a principal.

#### `admission.apiKeyWriters.users`

**Default:** `[]`

#### `admission.apiKeyWriters.groups`

**Default:** `[system:masters]`

### `admission.toolRouteWriters`

A group of 2 key(s).

Design 07 A6.15: who besides the operator may attach an HTTPRoute or a GRPCRoute to the assayd Gateway, on any listener BUT the serving listener `http`. An MCP tool route on a `tools` listener is what this is for (docs/install.md, section 6). Nothing in assayd emits tool routes, and assayd-gateway-routes refuses every other author, so with this empty no one can publish a tool through the Gateway without impersonating the operator.

What an identity here may write, and nothing more:

```
 * every parentRef naming the assayd Gateway carries a sectionName, and none
   is `http`. A parentRef with no sectionName attaches to every listener,
   the serving one included, so it is refused, with or without a port. So
   is an UPDATE that moves a route onto `http`, takes one off it, or
   removes its sectionName.
 * the route lists its hostnames, and none matches an Agent's serving host
   `<agent>.<namespace>.<gateway.hostnameSuffix>`: not the suffix, not a
   name under it, not a wildcard at or above it. On a listener that shares
   the serving port, a route with such a host would take that Agent's
   traffic, and could answer the policy compiler's 401 probe for it.
```

It grants NO RBAC. It only lifts the admission refusal: each identity still needs its own RBAC on the routes it writes -- `create` and `update`, and `patch` for `kubectl apply` -- and the listener's allowedRoutes must admit that namespace. It does not look at where a route sends traffic: an AgentgatewayBackend can name any address, an Agent's Service included, and design 07 A6.15 records that as open.

Never grant an identity here route RBAC in a run namespace, and never let a tool listener's allowedRoutes select one: a route there can name an Agent's revision Service directly and reach it with no `<agent>-auth`.

Unlike extraOperators, an identity here gains nothing else: it cannot write the reserved namespace labels, an AgentgatewayPolicy in a run namespace, or a key set. Empty -- the default -- admits no one but the operators, the operator's ServiceAccount and extraOperators, on any listener. Never list a group every identity carries, such as `system:authenticated` or `system:serviceaccounts`: any identity could then attach a tool route on any listener but `http` whose `allowedRoutes` admits its namespace, limited only by the hostname rule above and by RBAC. `http` would stay the operators'.

#### `admission.toolRouteWriters.users`

**Default:** `[]`

#### `admission.toolRouteWriters.groups`

**Default:** `[]`
